To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multi-laterally traded gas-heat-power market can be modeled and solved as a two-phase mixed integer linear programming problem.

the MLT-GHP model and the two-phase solution algorithm are developed to solve the market equilibrium of the coupled natural gas system, the district heating system, the power system, and their interdependency.
we propose a multi-lateral market trading model for coupled energy networks, and develop an algorithm to find the market clearing price and flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the multi-lateral market trading in a coupled energy network, and the proposed model and algorithm are expected to facilitate the operation and management of the multi-resource energy system.
the market trading of multi-resource energy networks, which is expected to provide a new perspective to the operation and planning of future energy system.
the market organization in multi-resource energy systems and provides a promising framework to address this challenging problem.

the multi-laterality in the energy trading market is an important feature of the emerging energy networks.
the MLT-GHP model and algorithm can be applied to a wide range of multi-resource energy networks to achieve efficient operation and optimal market organization.
the proposed multi-lateral trading scheme is a promising approach to promote the integration of energy systems, which is beneficial to the sustainable energy utilization.

the proposed multi-lateral trading scheme can effectively coordinate the interactions and interdependencies in coupled energy networks, and can be used as a reference for the market organization in the network-cogeneration systems.

the MLT-GHP model is capable of capturing the physical and economic interactions across the gas-heat-power networks and the market competition among energy suppliers, which provides a promising framework for the operation of integrated energy networks.

the multi-laterally coupled energy systems are more competitive and resilient than those of the single-resource system, and the multi-lateral market trading model can provide a better market equilibrium than the single-lateral one.
